back: Used for actions/events in the future that will happen soon [4].
Usually refers to something important, exciting, or very bad [4].
To say that something is expected to happen at a particular time [4].
To say that something is likely or certain to happen [4].
To say that something is ready to happen [4].
Used to give a reason for something, not to talk about the future [4].
aim, agree, expect, hope, intend, plan, promise, resolve [4].
Means 'planning a course of action' (common in speech/journalism) [4].
Used with 'I' and 'we' in future statements; more common to use 'll/won't [4].
Used with other subjects to mean 'must' (e.g., 'The match referee shall be...') [4].
